articles.summary: The AI company is gearing up for a potentially historic IPO, likely targeting mid-November for its Nasdaq debut. articles.title: Tech companies face mounting child safety lawsuits while pushing AI into schools
articles.summary: Snap confidentially settled a case claiming that its technology caused severe psychological distress to two teenage users. And Google was sued this week by the parents of a child who allegedly suffered a psychological crisis after chatting with the Gemini AI chatbot in Google Classroom. Concern is intensifying as artificial intelligence companies pursue trillion-dollar valuations, and established internet giants pour money into developing advanced AI models while pushing them into the classroom.

articles.title: Trump says U.S. carried out ‘minor strikes’ on Iran as missiles hit Qeshm Island
articles.summary: President Donald Trump told reporters Friday that the U.S. carried out "minor strikes" on Iran, amid reports that two missiles struck Qeshm Island near the Strait of Hormuz. The island lies off Iran's southern coast, near the Strait of Hormuz, the vital artery for oil and gas that has become a flashpoint in the war.

With the latest market turmoil, one investor said $1 trillion to $1.25 trillion is a more likely valuation target, although that could change with market conditions.

articles.title: OpenAI bugging suspect Alfozan pleads not guilty
articles.summary: The Saudi national charged with planting a listening device in the headquarters of OpenAI while he worked there pleaded not guilty on Friday during an appearance in San Francisco federal court. Abdulrahman Alfozan, 35, was sent back to jail after the brief hearing. Alfozan has been held without bail since his arrest on a criminal complaint in early October.

articles.title: Americans are on a 'treadmill of high inflation' and more rate hikes are likely, Fed's Daly says
articles.summary: San Francisco Federal Reserve President Mary Daly said Friday she expects the central bank will need to raise interest rates further, but joined her fellow policymakers in saying the pace and timing remain uncertain. "This has been high for too long, almost six years, and we're really starting to feel the burden of that spread everywhere." The policymaker said she's not concerned generally about economic growth but worried about the persistence of inflation.

articles.title: Data center double-down: Hassett says blue wave won't stop AI build-out
articles.summary: National Economic Council Director Kevin Hassett said Friday he expects data center growth to continue as projected, despite the blue-wave election that saw voters overwhelmingly favor limiting the tech infrastructure buildout. Hassett, on CNBC's "Squawk on the Street," acknowledged the dozens of measures on states' midterm ballots seeking to constrain data centers, a crucial part of President Donald Trump's push to win the global artificial intelligence race.

articles.title: OpenAI, Arm and Qualcomm executives react to post-midterm AI sell-off
articles.summary: In response to a Democratic sweep of Congress as well as a sizeable number of state governorships and legislatures in the midterm election Tuesday night, stocks initially rallied Wednesday, posting their best day in more than 18 months as President Trump accepted the blowout results with little fanfare.

Traditional oil and gas majors sank, while solar and green energy stocks surged, driven by expectations that a Democratic Congress will resume pushing subsidies for them.
